hints.title: DAG Path Enumeration Obstacle
hints.text: Finding all paths from vertex 0 to n - 1 in a directed acyclic graph requires exploring every branch without getting stuck in cycles. How does acyclic topological order guarantee termination?

hints.title: Acyclic Path Extension Invariant
hints.text: Because the graph is a directed acyclic graph (DAG), visited tracking is unnecessary. Every vertex on the current path strictly precedes its descendants.

hints.title: Recursive Branch Collection Procedure
hints.text: Define a recursive helper taking vertex u and path list. If u == n - 1, append a copy of path to results. Otherwise, iterate over all neighbors v in graph[u], append v to path, recurse on v, then pop v.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of vertices in graph (1 <= N <= 15)
complexity.notes: At most 2^(N-1) paths in a complete DAG, each taking O(N) time to copy.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Unbounded graph searches risk infinite loops, but DAG property guarantees finite paths.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Path buffer of size N requires O(N) recursion memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Explaining why DAG guarantees termination without an explicit visited set.
